```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
set.seed(1)
```

```{r}
library(regcompR)
n <- 300
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), g = factor(rep(1:30, each = 10)))
d$y <- rnbinom(n, mu = exp(1 + 0.4 * d$x + rnorm(30, 0, 0.4)[d$g]), size = 2)
f1 <- regcomp(y ~ x, family = "poisson", data = d)
f2 <- regcomp(y ~ x + (1 | g), phi ~ x, family = "nb2", data = d)
```

## Regression tables

`regcomp_table()` puts one or several fits side by side. Rows are grouped
by distribution parameter (each parameter has its own regression), random
effects are reported as standard deviations and correlations, and fit
statistics close the table. In a document chunk the table renders as a
formatted HTML, LaTeX or Word table, in R Markdown and Quarto alike:

```{r}
tab <- regcomp_table(Poisson = f1, `NB mixed` = f2, exponentiate = TRUE, stars = TRUE)
tab
```

In the console the same object prints as text:

```{r}
print(tab)
```

`show = "se"` gives standard errors instead of intervals; `conf.level`,
`digits` and `stats` control the rest. For Bayesian fits the table shows
posterior means with credible intervals, the number of draws and the
largest R-hat.

```{r}
regcomp_table(f1, f2, show = "se", stats = c("nobs", "AIC"))
```

`standardize = TRUE` reports each coefficient per standard deviation of
its covariate, and `vcov = "sandwich"` or `"quasi"` changes the standard
errors. `coef_plot()` draws the estimates of several fits side by side:

```{r, fig.height = 3}
coef_plot(Poisson = f1, `NB mixed` = f2, exponentiate = TRUE)
```

## Tidy output

`tidy()`, `glance()` and `augment()` methods follow the broom conventions,
so every package built on them works with regcompR fits: broom,
modelsummary, gtsummary, and others. `tidy()` adds a `component` column
naming the distribution parameter.

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("broom", quietly = TRUE)}
broom::tidy(f2)
broom::glance(f2)
head(broom::augment(f1))
```

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("modelsummary", quietly = TRUE)}
modelsummary::modelsummary(list(Poisson = f1, NB = f2), shape = term + component ~ model,
                           output = "markdown")
```

## Export

`export_table()` writes a table, a fit or a list of fits to a file whose
format follows the extension: `.csv`, `.html`, `.tex`, `.md` or `.docx`
(Word, with the flextable package). `export_plot()` saves any diagnostic
plot as `.png`, `.jpeg`, `.tiff`, `.pdf` or `.svg`.

```{r}
out <- tempdir()
export_table(tab, file.path(out, "models.html"))
export_table(list(f1, f2), file.path(out, "models.csv"), show = "se")
export_plot(f2, file.path(out, "qq.png"), which = "qq", width = 6, height = 4)
list.files(out, pattern = "models|qq")
```
